title: Fagin’s binary-relation spectrum problem
area: Database theory and finite model theory
formal: For every first-order sentence phi in a finite vocabulary, is there a first-order sentence psi using only equality and one binary relation symbol R such that \[\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi)=\operatorname{Spec}(\psi)\,?\]
definitions:
Use classical first-order logic with equality interpreted as actual identity. A finite structure has a nonempty domain. The spectrum Spec(phi) is the set of positive integers n for which some n-element structure satisfies phi. The input vocabulary may contain finitely many relation symbols, function symbols and constants of finite arities; all functions are total. Each sentence uses only finitely many symbols.

The output vocabulary has no nonlogical symbols except the binary relation R. R is arbitrary: loops, asymmetry and pairs of both orientations are allowed, so it need not be a simple undirected graph. Equality and logical connectives and quantifiers remain available. The same n must belong to both spectra for every positive integer n, including small sizes. There is no padding, multiplication of cardinality, finite exceptional set or asymptotic equivalence. The question asks existence of a sentence, without imposing an effective translation or a formula-length bound.
answer_criterion: Prove the exact spectrum-preservation theorem in Lean, or produce a first-order sentence whose spectrum is provably not the spectrum of any equality-plus-one-binary-relation sentence. A graph encoding that changes the domain size does not establish the theorem.
context: The spectrum survey records this as Fagin’s problem for binary relations. It asks how far vocabulary can be reduced while preserving model sizes, which is stricter than ordinary encodability of structures.
why: This asks whether a minimal relational vocabulary suffices to express all finite-model cardinality phenomena.

import_provenance.original_statement: Can every first-order spectrum be represented by a sentence whose vocabulary consists of just one binary relation? The set of finite-model sizes must be preserved exactly, so encodings that merely rescale the sizes do not settle the question.

sentences: A sentence’s spectrum records the sizes of its finite nonempty models.

Equality remains available and the binary relation need not describe a simple graph.
